concept_summary: Initial device setup involves configuring basic parameters like hostname, management IP addressing, user accounts, and login banners. These foundational settings establish device identity and enable remote management access. The hostname appears in CLI prompts and configuration filenames, while management interfaces provide out-of-band access for administration.
cli_mode_context: Enter privileged EXEC mode with 'enable', then global configuration mode with 'configure terminal'. Basic setup commands are executed directly in global config mode.
example_commands:
configure terminal
hostname CoreSwitch01
ip domain-name example.com
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description Management Interface
 ip address 192.0.2.10 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
username admin privilege 15 secret Str0ngP@ssw0rd
banner motd #
Authorized Access Only
Unauthorized access is prohibited
#
end

key_parameters.description: Sets the device hostname displayed in CLI prompt
Configures DNS domain name for the device
Creates local user account with privilege level (0-15, where 15 is full admin)
Sets encrypted password using stronger encryption than 'password' command
Message-of-the-day banner shown at login (delimited by # or other character)

concept_summary: Physical and logical interface configuration defines port parameters including speed, duplex, descriptions, and Layer 2/Layer 3 addressing. Interfaces can operate in switchport mode (Layer 2) or routed mode (Layer 3). Configuration includes enabling/disabling interfaces, assigning IP addresses, and setting media-specific parameters like auto-negotiation.
cli_mode_context: From global config mode, enter interface configuration with 'interface <type><slot>/<port>' (e.g., 'interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1'). Use 'no switchport' to convert from Layer 2 to Layer 3 mode.
example_commands:
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 description Uplink to Distribution Layer
 no switchport
 ip address 192.0.2.1 255.255.255.252
 speed 1000
 duplex full
 no shutdown
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/2
 description Access Port VLAN 10
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
end

key_parameters.description: Converts interface from Layer 2 switchport to Layer 3 routed port
Assigns IPv4 address and subnet mask to Layer 3 interface

concept_summary: VLANs segment switched networks into logical broadcast domains independent of physical topology. Each VLAN forms a separate Layer 2 domain with its own spanning-tree instance in PVST mode. Trunks carry multiple VLANs between switches using 802.1Q tagging, while access ports belong to a single untagged VLAN. VTP can distribute VLAN configuration across devices in the same domain.
cli_mode_context: Create VLANs in global config with 'vlan <id>' command, then configure interface mode with 'switchport mode access|trunk' in interface config. VLANs 1 and 1002-1005 are reserved and cannot be deleted.
example_commands:
configure terminal
vlan 10
 name Engineering
vlan 20
 name Sales
vlan 30
 name Management
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/5
 description Access port for Engineering
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24
 description Trunk to distribution switch
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
end

key_parameters.description: Configures port as access port carrying single untagged VLAN
Configures port as trunk carrying multiple tagged VLANs
Assigns access port to specific VLAN
Restricts which VLANs are permitted on trunk (default is all)
Sets untagged VLAN for 802.1Q trunk (default VLAN 1)

concept_summary: Static routes are manually configured forwarding entries that define explicit paths to destination networks. They provide deterministic routing behavior and are commonly used for default routes, stub networks, or backup paths. Static routes have administrative distance of 1 by default, making them preferred over most dynamic routing protocols.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes in global configuration mode using 'ip route' command with destination network, mask, and next-hop or exit interface.

key_parameters.description: IP address of next-hop router for this destination
Local interface to use for reaching destination
Optional AD value (1-255) to prefer/deprioritize route
Null interface for blackhole routing (discards traffic)

concept_summary: OSPF is a link-state interior gateway protocol that uses Dijkstra's shortest path first algorithm to build routing tables. It supports hierarchical network design through areas, fast convergence, and VLSM/CIDR. OSPF routers form adjacencies with neighbors and exchange link-state advertisements to maintain synchronized topology databases. Cisco IOS-XE supports both OSPFv2 for IPv4 and OSPFv3 for IPv6.
cli_mode_context: Enable OSPF with 'router ospf <process-id>' in global config mode, then use 'network' statements to identify interfaces participating in OSPF by matching IP addresses with wildcard masks and associating them with areas.
example_commands:
configure terminal
router ospf 1
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 network 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
 network 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255 area 10
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 default-information originate
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 ip ospf 1 area 0
 ip ospf network point-to-point
 ip ospf hello-interval 5
 ip ospf cost 10
end

key_parameters.description: Enables OSPF routing with locally significant process ID (1-65535)
Manually sets OSPF router ID (recommended, otherwise derived from highest loopback or interface IP)
Matches interfaces by wildcard and assigns them to OSPF area
Prevents OSPF hello packets on interface while still advertising network
Advertises default route into OSPF domain
Enables simple password authentication for area

concept_summary: BGP is an exterior gateway protocol used for inter-AS routing on the Internet and in large enterprise networks. It is a path-vector protocol that makes routing decisions based on paths, network policies, and rule-sets. BGP supports IBGP (within an AS) and EBGP (between different ASes). Key attributes include AS_PATH, LOCAL_PREF, MED, and NEXT_HOP used in the BGP best-path selection algorithm.
cli_mode_context: Enable BGP with 'router bgp <as-number>' in global config, then define networks to advertise and configure neighbors. Use 'network' command to originate prefixes and 'neighbor' commands to establish peering sessions.
example_commands:
configure terminal
ip routing
router bgp 65001
 bgp router-id 192.0.2.1
 bgp log-neighbor-changes
 network 192.0.2.0 mask 255.255.255.0
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 description EBGP to ISP
 neighbor 203.0.113.1 remote-as 65001
 neighbor 203.0.113.1 update-source Loopback0
 neighbor 203.0.113.1 next-hop-self
 address-family ipv4
  neighbor 198.51.100.1 activate
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 activate
end

key_parameters.description: Enables BGP with AS number (1-65535, 64512-65535 are private)
Advertises network into BGP (must exist in routing table)
Defines BGP neighbor and their AS number (IBGP if same, EBGP if different)
Source interface for BGP session (important for IBGP with loopbacks)
Sets local router as next-hop for routes advertised to this neighbor

concept_summary: EIGRP is a Cisco proprietary advanced distance-vector routing protocol using DUAL algorithm for fast convergence and loop prevention. It supports unequal-cost load balancing and automatic summarization. IS-IS is a link-state protocol originally designed for OSI networks, now commonly used in large service provider networks. Both protocols offer alternative routing solutions to OSPF with different operational characteristics.
cli_mode_context: For EIGRP, use 'router eigrp <as-number>' in global config. Modern deployments may use named mode with 'router eigrp <name>'. IS-IS requires 'router isis <tag>' and NET address configuration.
example_commands:
configure terminal
router eigrp 100
 network 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255
 network 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255
 eigrp router-id 192.0.2.1
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 no auto-summary
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 ip hello-interval eigrp 100 3
 ip hold-time eigrp 100 10
end

key_parameters.description: Enables EIGRP with AS number (must match between neighbors)
Enables EIGRP on interfaces matching the network range
Suppresses EIGRP hello packets while still advertising network
Disables automatic route summarization at classful boundaries

concept_summary: First-hop redundancy protocols provide gateway redundancy for end hosts by allowing multiple routers to share a virtual IP address. HSRP (Hot Standby Router Protocol) and VRRP (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol) elect an active router that handles traffic while standby routers monitor and take over upon failure. This ensures continuous connectivity even when individual routers fail.
cli_mode_context: Configure HSRP or VRRP on Layer 3 interfaces using 'standby' commands for HSRP or 'vrrp' commands for VRRP in interface configuration mode. Multiple groups can coexist on the same interface.
example_commands:
configure terminal
interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.0.2.2 255.255.255.0
 standby 1 ip 192.0.2.1
 standby 1 priority 110
 standby 1 preempt
 standby 1 authentication md5 key-string MySecretKey
interface Vlan20
 ip address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.0
 vrrp 1 ip 198.51.100.1
 vrrp 1 priority 110
 vrrp 1 preempt
end

key_parameters.description: Configures HSRP group and virtual IP address
Sets HSRP priority (0-255, default 100, highest becomes active)
Allows higher priority router to reclaim active role
Configures VRRP group and virtual IP

concept_summary: Access Control Lists filter traffic based on packet headers including source/destination IP, protocol, and port numbers. Standard ACLs (1-99, 1300-1999) filter only on source IP, while extended ACLs (100-199, 2000-2699) filter on multiple criteria. Named ACLs provide better documentation. ACLs are applied to interfaces directionally and process packets top-down until a match is found, with implicit deny at the end.
cli_mode_context: Create ACL with 'access-list <number>' for numbered or 'ip access-list {standard|extended} <name>' for named. Apply to interfaces with 'ip access-group <name> {in|out}' in interface config mode.
example_commands:
configure terminal
ip access-list extended BLOCK_TELNET
 10 deny tcp any any eq 23 log
 20 permit ip any any
ip access-list extended PERMIT_WEB
 permit tcp 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 80
 permit tcp 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443
 deny ip any any log
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 ip access-group BLOCK_TELNET in
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/2
 ip access-group PERMIT_WEB out
end

key_parameters.description: Creates named ACL with better documentation
Action to take when packet matches this ACE
Protocol to match (ip matches all protocols)
Matches any source or destination address
Matches specific port number or name
Generates log messages for matched packets

verification_commands: show ip interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1 | include access list

concept_summary: Network Address Translation maps private IP addresses to public addresses enabling Internet connectivity for RFC 1918 networks. Static NAT provides one-to-one mappings, dynamic NAT uses address pools, and PAT (Port Address Translation or NAT overload) multiplexes multiple private addresses to single public address using port numbers. NAT improves address conservation and adds a layer of obscurity.
cli_mode_context: Define inside and outside interfaces with 'ip nat {inside|outside}', create address pools or static mappings in global config, and configure ACLs to identify traffic to be translated.
example_commands:
configure terminal
ip access-list standard NAT_INTERNAL
 permit 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255
ip nat pool PUBLIC_POOL 198.51.100.1 198.51.100.10 netmask 255.255.255.240
ip nat inside source list NAT_INTERNAL pool PUBLIC_POOL overload
ip nat inside source static 192.0.2.10 198.51.100.50
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description Inside Network
 ip nat inside
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description Outside Internet
 ip nat outside
end

key_parameters.description: Marks interface as inside (private network side)
Marks interface as outside (public network side)
Defines pool of public IP addresses for dynamic NAT

key_parameters.parameter: ip nat inside source list ... pool ... overload

key_parameters.description: Enables PAT/port translation for address conservation

concept_summary: IPsec provides secure IP communications through authentication and encryption. Site-to-site VPNs use IKE (Internet Key Exchange) to negotiate security associations and establish encrypted tunnels between networks. Configuration involves crypto policies for IKE phase 1, transform sets for phase 2, crypto ACLs to define interesting traffic, and crypto maps binding all elements together and applying to interfaces.
cli_mode_context: Define IKE policy with 'crypto isakmp policy', create IPsec transform sets with 'crypto ipsec transform-set', define traffic with crypto ACLs, create crypto map with 'crypto map', and apply map to interface.
example_commands:
configure terminal
crypto isakmp policy 10
 encryption aes 256
 hash sha256
 authentication pre-share
 group 14
crypto isakmp key MyPreSharedKey address 203.0.113.1
crypto ipsec transform-set STRONG esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac
 mode tunnel
ip access-list extended VPN_TRAFFIC
 permit ip 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.255 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255
crypto map SITE_TO_SITE 10 ipsec-isakmp
 set peer 203.0.113.1
 set transform-set STRONG
 match address VPN_TRAFFIC
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 crypto map SITE_TO_SITE
end

key_parameters.description: Defines phase 2 encryption and authentication algorithms
Encapsulating Security Payload with AES encryption
Binds peer, transform set, and traffic selectors
Specifies remote VPN endpoint IP address

concept_summary: Quality of Service mechanisms classify, mark, police, shape, and queue traffic to provide differential treatment based on application requirements. MQC (Modular QoS CLI) uses class-maps to classify traffic, policy-maps to define actions, and service-policy to apply policies to interfaces. Common actions include marking DSCP/CoS values, policing rates, shaping traffic, and assigning to priority or bandwidth queues.
cli_mode_context: Define traffic classes with 'class-map', specify QoS actions with 'policy-map', and apply policies to interfaces with 'service-policy {input|output}' in interface config mode.
example_commands:
configure terminal
class-map match-any VOICE
 match ip dscp ef
 match protocol rtp
class-map match-any CRITICAL_DATA
 match ip dscp af31
 match access-group name BUSINESS_APPS
policy-map WAN_EDGE
 class VOICE
  priority percent 30
  set dscp ef
 class CRITICAL_DATA
  bandwidth percent 40
  set dscp af31
 class class-default
  fair-queue
  random-detect
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 service-policy output WAN_EDGE
end

key_parameters.description: Specifies match conditions (protocol, ACL, DSCP, CoS, etc.)
Defines QoS actions to apply to classified traffic
Assigns class to low-latency queue (strict priority)
Buffers traffic to smooth bursts and conform to rate
Marks IP DSCP value for QoS treatment

concept_summary: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, Accounting) provides centralized access control using TACACS+ or RADIUS servers. Authentication verifies user identity, authorization determines permitted commands, and accounting logs user actions. Local AAA uses device-local username database as fallback. Method lists define the sequence of authentication sources (server groups then local) for different access types like console, VTY, and enable mode.
cli_mode_context: Enable AAA with 'aaa new-model' in global config, define server groups, create method lists for different login types, and apply to lines or enable mode.
example_commands:
configure terminal
aaa new-model
tacacs-server host 192.0.2.50 key TacacsSecret123
tacacs-server host 192.0.2.51 key TacacsSecret123
aaa group server tacacs+ TACACS_GROUP
 server 192.0.2.50
 server 192.0.2.51
aaa authentication login default group TACACS_GROUP local
aaa authentication enable default group TACACS_GROUP enable
aaa authorization exec default group TACACS_GROUP local
aaa authorization commands 15 default group TACACS_GROUP local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group TACACS_GROUP
aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group TACACS_GROUP
line vty 0 15
 login authentication default
end

key_parameters.description: Enables AAA access control (disables default authentication)
Defines TACACS+ server IP and shared secret
Creates named server group for method lists
Defines method list for login authentication
Defines authorization for EXEC shell access
Defines command authorization by privilege level
Configures accounting logging (start-stop logs session duration)
Applies authentication method list to line

concept_summary: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) enables remote monitoring and management via polling and traps. Syslog provides centralized logging with severity levels 0-7. SNMP versions include v1/v2c (community-based) and v3 (user-based with encryption). Logging can be directed to console, buffer, or remote syslog servers. Traps notify management stations of events while syslog provides detailed operational messages.
cli_mode_context: Configure SNMP with 'snmp-server' commands in global config. Configure logging with 'logging' commands specifying destinations and severity levels.
example_commands:
configure terminal
snmp-server community PublicRO ro
snmp-server community PrivateRW rw
snmp-server location DataCenter-01
snmp-server contact netadmin@example.com
snmp-server host 192.0.2.100 version 2c PublicRO
snmp-server enable traps snmp linkdown linkup
snmp-server enable traps config
logging buffered 16384 informational
logging console warnings
logging host 192.0.2.200
logging trap informational
logging source-interface Loopback0
service timestamps log datetime msec localtime show-timezone
end

key_parameters.description: Sets SNMP v1/v2c community string with ro (read-only) or rw (read-write)
Defines NMS host to receive SNMP traps
Enables specific trap types to be sent
Enables local log buffer with size and severity level
Sends logs to remote syslog server
Sets severity level for syslog messages (0-7)

concept_summary: VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) overlays Layer 2 networks over Layer 3 infrastructure using MAC-in-UDP encapsulation. It addresses VLAN scalability limitations by supporting 16 million network segments. EVPN (Ethernet VPN) provides the control plane for VXLAN using BGP to distribute MAC/IP reachability information. This architecture enables large-scale multi-tenancy in data centers with optimized forwarding and mobility.
cli_mode_context: Configure VXLAN Network Virtualization Endpoint (VTEP) with 'interface nve' for tunnel interface, define VNI-to-VLAN mappings, and configure EVPN BGP for control plane. Requires underlay IP reachability.
example_commands:
configure terminal
feature nve
feature vn-segment-vlan-based
vlan 10
 vn-segment 10010
interface nve1
 no shutdown
 source-interface Loopback0
 member vni 10010
  mcast-group 239.0.0.10
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 remote-as 65001
 address-family l2vpn evpn
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 send-community extended
evpn
 vni 10010 l2
  rd auto
  route-target import auto
  route-target export auto
end

key_parameters.description: Specifies source interface for VXLAN tunnel (typically loopback)
Associates VXLAN Network Identifier with NVE interface
Maps VLAN to VNI (VXLAN segment ID)
Specifies multicast group for BUM traffic in flood-and-learn mode
Enables EVPN address family in BGP for control plane

reason: VXLAN/EVPN is primarily supported on Nexus platforms; Catalyst IOS-XE switches in release 17.15.x have limited or no native VXLAN/EVPN support. This feature requires Nexus 9000 series documentation.

concept_summary: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) uses labels to forward packets through the network, enabling traffic engineering, VPNs, and fast reroute. LDP distributes labels automatically, while RSVP-TE provides explicit path control. MPLS L3VPNs (RFC 4364) use VRF instances with route distinguishers and route targets to separate customer routing tables on provider PE routers.
cli_mode_context: Enable MPLS globally with 'mpls ip' in global config and on interfaces. Configure LDP with 'mpls label protocol ldp' and 'mpls ldp router-id'. For L3VPNs, create VRFs with 'ip vrf' and configure BGP VPNv4 address family.
example_commands:
configure terminal
mpls label protocol ldp
mpls ldp router-id Loopback0 force
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 ip address 192.0.2.1 255.255.255.252
 mpls ip
ip vrf CUSTOMER_A
 rd 65001:100
 route-target export 65001:100
 route-target import 65001:100
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 ip vrf forwarding CUSTOMER_A
 ip address 198.51.100.1 255.255.255.0
router bgp 65001
 address-family vpnv4
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 send-community extended
 address-family ipv4 vrf CUSTOMER_A
  redistribute connected
end

Configures Label Distribution Protocol for label exchange
Sets LDP router ID (should be stable loopback)
Creates VRF instance for L3VPN customer separation
Route Distinguisher makes VPN routes globally unique (AS:nn or IP:nn format)
Route Target controls VPN route import/export (community-based filtering)
Enables BGP VPNv4 address family for L3VPN

concept_summary: High availability features ensure continuous operation during hardware or software failures. StackWise technology allows multiple physical switches to operate as single logical unit with unified management plane. SSO (Stateful Switchover) maintains protocol state during supervisor failover. NSF (Nonstop Forwarding) keeps data plane forwarding during control plane restarts. Redundant supervisors, power supplies, and fans provide hardware resilience.
cli_mode_context: StackWise configuration occurs automatically when switches are cabled together. Switch priority is set with 'switch <number> priority <value>'. NSF is enabled per protocol (e.g., 'nsf cisco' in OSPF config). Redundancy mode is typically auto-configured.
example_commands:
configure terminal
switch 1 priority 15
switch 1 renumber 1
switch 2 priority 14
switch 2 renumber 2
stack-mac persistent timer 0
redundancy
 mode sso
router ospf 1
 nsf cisco
router bgp 65001
 bgp graceful-restart
end

key_parameters.description: Sets stack member priority (1-15, highest becomes stack master)
Controls stack MAC address persistence (0 = never change)
Enables Stateful Switchover for supervisor redundancy
Enables Cisco NSF for graceful restart (OSPF example)

verification_commands: show platform software redundancy switch active

concept_summary: System management includes configuration backup and restore, software upgrade procedures, licensing management, and file system operations. Running-config is active configuration in RAM, while startup-config in NVRAM loads at boot. Software images are stored in flash and can be upgraded using install mode or bundle mode. Smart Licensing connects to Cisco cloud for automated license management, while traditional licenses use PAK codes.
cli_mode_context: Use 'copy' commands to save/restore configurations between running-config, startup-config, and remote servers (TFTP, FTP, SCP). Use 'install' or 'archive download-sw' for software upgrades. License management uses 'license' commands.
example_commands:
configure terminal
archive
 path tftp://192.0.2.50/config-backups/$h-
 write-memory
license boot level network-advantage
end
copy running-config startup-config
copy startup-config tftp://192.0.2.50/backup-config.txt
copy tftp://192.0.2.50/restore-config.txt running-config
install add file bootflash:cat9k-universalk9.17.15.01.SPA.bin activate commit
dir bootflash:
show version
show license summary
show license all

concept_summary: IOS-XR uses a commit-based configuration model where changes are staged and must be explicitly committed to take effect. Initial setup includes hostname, domain configuration, management interface addressing, and user creation. Unlike IOS/IOS-XE, configuration changes are not applied immediately but are validated and committed as a transaction, allowing rollback if needed.
cli_mode_context: Enter configuration mode with 'configure' or 'config' command. Make configuration changes, then use 'commit' to apply them. Use 'show configuration' to view uncommitted changes before committing.
example_commands:
configure
hostname PE-Router01
domain name example.com
interface MgmtEth0/RP0/CPU0/0
 ipv4 address 192.0.2.10 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
username admin
 group root-lr
 group cisco-support
 secret Str0ngP@ss
banner motd ;
Authorized Access Only - PE-Router01
;
commit
end

Applies staged configuration changes to active configuration
Assigns user to root-level read group for admin access
Sets encrypted password for user account

concept_summary: IOS-XR handles Layer 2 services primarily through L2VPN constructs rather than traditional VLAN switching. Bridge domains provide Layer 2 forwarding within a router, while L2VPN services like VPWS and VPLS extend Layer 2 connectivity across MPLS networks. concept_summary: OSPF in IOS-XR operates as a link-state IGP with area hierarchy and SPF path calculation. Configuration uses a process-name rather than process-ID, and interfaces are explicitly added to areas. IOS-XR supports both OSPFv2 for IPv4 and OSPFv3 for IPv6, with advanced features like NSR for hitless failover and graceful restart for control-plane resilience.
cli_mode_context: Configure OSPF with 'router ospf <process-name>' and explicitly assign areas to interfaces. Use 'area <area-id>' context to configure area parameters.
example_commands:
configure
router ospf CORE
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 nsr
 area 0
  interface Loopback0

Interfaces support routed (no switchport) or switched modes. Configuration includes speed, duplex, descriptions, and L2/L3 parameters. EOS excels at high-density 100G/400G interfaces with advanced buffering and telemetry.

interface Ethernet1

 no switchport

 mtu 9214
 no shutdown
interface Ethernet2
 description Server-Port
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 100
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
interface Vlan100
 description SVI-for-Servers
 ip address 198.51.100.1/24
 ip virtual-router address 198.51.100.254
interface Loopback0
 ip address 192.0.2.100/32
end

SVI (VLAN interfaces) provide inter-VLAN routing. EOS adds virtual-router MAC for consistent gateway across MLAG pairs. Rapid-PVST+ or MST provide loop prevention.

vlan 20

vlan 100

interface Ethernet10

interface Vlan10

concept_summary: EOS static routes use IOS syntax with destination, mask, next-hop or interface, and administrative distance. IPv4 and IPv6 static routes supported. VRF-aware routing enables multi-tenancy. Track objects provide conditional routing based on reachability. Static routes integrate with BFD for fast failure detection.
cli_mode_context: Configure static routes with 'ip route' in config mode. Specify destination, mask, next-hop/interface, and optional distance.
example_commands:
configure
ip route 0.0.0.0/0 192.0.2.1
ip route 198.51.100.0/24 Ethernet1
ip route 203.0.113.0/24 192.0.2.5 10
ip route 203.0.113.128/25 Null0
ipv6 route ::/0 2001:DB8::1
ip route vrf CUSTOMER-A 10.0.0.0/8 198.51.100.1
end

concept_summary: EOS OSPF implements OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 with area hierarchy and IOS-like syntax. Configuration includes process ID, router ID, network statements, and area parameters. EOS adds BFD integration for sub-second failover. Supports authentication, graceful restart, and ECMP. Multi-instance OSPF per VRF.
cli_mode_context: Enable OSPF with 'router ospf <process-id>' in config mode. Use 'network' statements or interface-level configuration.
example_commands:
configure
router ospf 1
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 network 192.0.2.0/24 area 0.0.0.0
 network 198.51.100.0/24 area 0.0.0.10
 passive-interface default
 no passive-interface Ethernet1
 max-lsas 12000
 distance ospf external 110
interface Ethernet1
 ip ospf network point-to-point
 ip ospf cost 100
 ip ospf area 0.0.0.0
 ip ospf bfd
end

concept_summary: EOS BGP supports IBGP, EBGP, and advanced features like route reflection, confederation, and add-path. Configuration uses IOS syntax with neighbor statements and address families. EOS excels at large-scale BGP with EVPN for data center fabrics. Supports diverse AFIs including IPv4, IPv6, EVPN, and VPNv4. BGP unnumbered simplifies configuration using IPv6 link-local addressing.
cli_mode_context: Configure BGP with 'router bgp <as-number>' in config mode. Define neighbors and activate address families.
example_commands:
configure
router bgp 65001
 router-id 192.0.2.1
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 description EBGP-ISP
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 remote-as 65001
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 update-source Loopback0
 neighbor 192.0.2.254 next-hop-self
 network 192.0.2.0/24
 address-family ipv4
  neighbor 198.51.100.1 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
 address-family evpn
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.254 send-community extended
end

concept_summary: EOS does not support EIGRP as it is Cisco proprietary. IS-IS support is available for service provider deployments with Level-1/Level-2 hierarchy. RIP exists for legacy compatibility. Modern EOS deployments favor OSPF and BGP especially for EVPN-VXLAN data center fabrics.
cli_mode_context: Configure IS-IS with 'router isis' if needed. Most modern deployments use BGP for underlay/overlay.
example_commands:
configure
router isis CORE
 net 49.0001.0192.0000.2001.00
 is-type level-2
 address-family ipv4 unicast
interface Ethernet1
 isis enable CORE
 isis network point-to-point
end
reason: EIGRP not supported (Cisco proprietary). IS-IS available but uncommon in EOS deployments focused on data center BGP/EVPN. RIP exists but legacy only.

concept_summary: EOS supports VRRP for first-hop redundancy with virtual IP addressing. mlag configuration

end

concept_summary: EOS ACLs use IOS syntax with standard and extended lists for traffic filtering. ACLs match on Layer 3/4 headers with permit/deny actions. IPv4 and IPv6 ACLs supported. Control-plane ACL protects management plane. EOS adds object-groups and time-based ACLs. Applied to interfaces, line VTY, or control-plane.
cli_mode_context: Create ACLs with 'ip access-list' in config mode. Apply to interfaces with 'ip access-group'. Use sequence numbers for ordering.
example_commands:

ip access-list standard MGMT-ACCESS
 10 permit 192.0.2.0/24
 20 deny any log
ip access-list extended BLOCK-TELNET
 10 deny tcp any any eq telnet log
 20 permit ip any any
interface Ethernet10

line vty 0 4

ipv6 access-list IPV6-FILTER
 10 deny ipv6 any any fragments
 20 permit ipv6 2001:DB8::/32 any
 30 deny ipv6 any any log
end

concept_summary: EOS NAT supports source NAT, destination NAT, and static NAT for address translation. Configuration includes NAT pools, inside/outside interfaces, and translation rules. ip access-list standard NAT-INTERNAL

interface Vlan10

interface Ethernet1

end

concept_summary: EOS supports IPsec VPN for site-to-site connectivity with IKEv1/IKEv2. Configuration includes crypto maps, IKE policies, transform sets, and access lists defining interesting traffic. Both tunnel and transport modes supported. Integration with dynamic routing over VPN. CloudVision provides centralized VPN management.
cli_mode_context: Configure IPsec with 'crypto' commands similar to IOS. Define IKE policy, transform set, crypto map, and apply to interface.
example_commands:
configure
crypto isakmp policy 10
 encryption aes 256
 hash sha256
 authentication pre-share
 group 14
crypto isakmp key MyPreSharedKey address 203.0.113.1
crypto ipsec transform-set STRONG esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac
ip access-list extended VPN-TRAFFIC
 permit ip 192.0.2.0/24 198.51.100.0/24
crypto map SITE-TO-SITE 10 ipsec-isakmp
 set peer 203.0.113.1
 set transform-set STRONG
 match address VPN-TRAFFIC
interface Ethernet1
 crypto map SITE-TO-SITE
end

concept_summary: EOS QoS uses modular framework with class-maps, policy-maps, and service-policies. Hardware-based QoS leverages merchant silicon capabilities. Configuration includes classification, marking, policing, shaping, and queueing. DSCP-based and CoS-based QoS supported. EOS provides granular queue control with weighted round-robin and strict priority.
cli_mode_context: Define class-maps for classification, policy-maps for actions, apply with service-policy to interfaces.
example_commands:
configure
class-map match-any VOICE
 match ip dscp ef
class-map match-any CRITICAL
 match ip dscp af31
policy-map QOS-OUT
 class VOICE
  priority level 1
  police rate 2 mbps
 class CRITICAL
  bandwidth percent 40
 class class-default
  bandwidth percent 20
interface Ethernet1
 service-policy output QOS-OUT
qos cos 5
end
